## orgs

Organizations, members and teams.

### `forgejo_list_orgs`

**List organizations**

List organizations: the ones you belong to (omit `username`), or the public organizations of another user. Use forgejo_get_org for details of one organization and forgejo_list_repos with owner=<org> for its repositories.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | No | List this user's organizations. Omit for your own. |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_get_org`

**Get organization details**

Get details of one organization: full name, description, website, location, email and visibility. Use forgejo_list_org_members and forgejo_list_teams for its people, and forgejo_list_repos with owner=<org> for its repositories.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization name (e.g. "acme") |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_create_org`

**Create an organization**

Create a new organization owned by the authenticated user (who becomes a member of its Owners team). Afterwards, create teams with forgejo_create_team and repositories with forgejo_create_repo (owner=<org>). Some instances only let admins create organizations.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (creates something)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Yes | Organization name, used in URLs (letters, digits, "-", "_" and ".") |
| `full_name` | string | No | Display name |
| `description` | string | No | Short description |
| `website` | string | No | Website URL |
| `location` | string | No | Location |
| `email` | string | No | Public contact email |
| `visibility` | `public` \| `limited` \| `private` | No | "public": visible to everyone; "limited": signed-in users only; "private": members only |
| `repo_admin_change_team_access` | boolean | No | Let repository admins add or remove team access to their repositories |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_update_org`

**Update organization settings**

Change an organization's profile and settings: full name, description, website, location, email, visibility and whether repository admins can change team access. Only the fields you pass are changed. Requires organization owner rights.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (idempotent update)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization name (e.g. "acme") |
| `full_name` | string | No | Display name |
| `description` | string | No | Short description (an empty string clears it) |
| `website` | string | No | Website URL |
| `location` | string | No | Location |
| `email` | string | No | Public contact email |
| `visibility` | `public` \| `limited` \| `private` | No | "public": visible to everyone; "limited": signed-in users only; "private": members only |
| `repo_admin_change_team_access` | boolean | No | Let repository admins add or remove team access to their repositories |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_delete_org`

**Delete an organization**

Permanently delete an organization. Forgejo refuses while it still owns repositories or packages (delete or transfer them first). This cannot be undone. As a safety check, `confirm_name` must repeat the organization name exactly; only call this after the user has explicitly confirmed which organization to delete.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization to delete |
| `confirm_name` | string | Yes | Must be exactly the same as `org`, to confirm the deletion |

### `forgejo_list_org_members`

**List organization members**

List the members of an organization. If you are not a member yourself, only members who made their membership public are shown. Use forgejo_list_teams to see how members are grouped, and forgejo_update_team_members to change team membership.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization name (e.g. "acme") |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_remove_org_member`

**Remove an organization member**

Remove a user from an organization: they leave every team in it and lose access to its private repositories. Requires organization owner rights. To only take someone out of one team, use forgejo_update_team_members instead.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization name (e.g. "acme") |
| `username` | string | Yes | User to remove |

### `forgejo_list_teams`

**List organization teams**

List the teams of an organization with their ID, permission level, repository units and whether they cover all repositories. Pass `query` to search team names (and descriptions). Team IDs and names are used by forgejo_update_team_members and forgejo_update_team_repos; create teams with forgejo_create_team.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization name (e.g. "acme") |
| `query` | string | No | Only teams whose name (or description) contains this text |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_create_team`

**Create a team**

Create a team in an organization with a permission level ("read", "write" or "admin") applied to a set of repository units. By default the team gets that permission on code, issues, pulls, releases, wiki, projects, packages, actions; pass `units` to choose others, or `units_map` for a different level per unit. Then add people with forgejo_update_team_members and (unless includes_all_repositories) repositories with forgejo_update_team_repos.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (creates something)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization name (e.g. "acme") |
| `name` | string | Yes | Team name, e.g. "developers" |
| `description` | string | No | Short description |
| `permission` | `read` \| `write` \| `admin` | No | Access level on the team's repositories (default "read"). "admin" grants full access to every unit and ignores units/units_map. Default: `"read"`. |
| `units` | string[] | No | Repository units the permission applies to: repo.code, repo.issues, repo.pulls, repo.releases, repo.wiki, repo.projects, repo.packages, repo.actions, repo.ext_issues, repo.ext_wiki (default: all of these except the two ext_ ones) |
| `units_map` | object (map) | No | Per-unit access instead of one level, e.g. {"repo.code": "read", "repo.issues": "write"}. Overrides permission and units. |
| `includes_all_repositories` | boolean | No | Give the team access to all current and future repositories of the organization. Default: `false`. |
| `can_create_org_repo` | boolean | No | Let team members create repositories in the organization. Default: `false`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_update_team_members`

**Add or remove team members**

Add users to and/or remove users from an organization team (given by ID or name). Adding someone to a team also makes them a member of the organization. Each user is processed separately and the result lists what succeeded and what failed. Use forgejo_list_teams to find teams and forgejo_remove_org_member to remove someone from the whole organization.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (idempotent update)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization that owns the team |
| `team` | integer \| string | Yes | The team: its numeric ID, or its name within the organization (e.g. "developers") |
| `add` | string[] | No | Usernames to add to the team |
| `remove` | string[] | No | Usernames to remove from the team |

### `forgejo_update_team_repos`

**Add or remove team repositories**

Give an organization team access to repositories, or take it away (team by ID or name; repositories by name, all in the same organization). Each repository is processed separately and the result lists what succeeded and what failed. Not needed for teams created with includes_all_repositories. Use forgejo_list_teams to find teams.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (idempotent update)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org` | string | Yes | Organization that owns the team and the repositories |
| `team` | integer \| string | Yes | The team: its numeric ID, or its name within the organization (e.g. "developers") |
| `add` | string[] | No | Repository names to give the team access to (e.g. "website" or "acme/website") |
| `remove` | string[] | No | Repository names to remove from the team |

---

## repo_admin

Collaborators, branch protection, webhooks, mirrors and repository deletion.

### `forgejo_delete_repo`

**Delete a repository**

PERMANENTLY delete a repository with all its code, branches, issues, pull requests, releases, wiki, packages links and settings. This CANNOT be undone. Only call it when the user explicitly asked to delete this exact repository, and set `confirm_full_name` to "owner/repo" (it must match owner and repo exactly). To keep the data but make it read-only, use forgejo_update_repo with archived: true instead.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `confirm_full_name` | string | Yes | Safety check: the full repository name "owner/repo" again. Nothing is deleted unless it matches owner and repo exactly |

### `forgejo_list_collaborators`

**List repository collaborators**

List the users added as collaborators on a repository. With `include_permissions`, also look up each one's access level (read/write/admin; at most 20 lookups per call). The owner and organization team members have access without being listed here. Use forgejo_set_collaborator to add or change access and forgejo_remove_collaborator to revoke it.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `include_permissions` | boolean | No | Also look up each collaborator's permission (one extra request per user, first 20 only) Default: `false`. |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_set_collaborator`

**Add a collaborator or change their access**

Add a user as a collaborator on a repository, or change an existing collaborator's access level: "read" (view and clone), "write" (push, manage issues and pull requests) or "admin" (also settings, collaborators and webhooks). Use forgejo_list_collaborators to see current collaborators and forgejo_remove_collaborator to revoke access.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (idempotent update)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `username` | string | Yes | User name of the person to add or update |
| `permission` | `read` \| `write` \| `admin` | Yes | Access level: "read", "write" or "admin" |

### `forgejo_remove_collaborator`

**Remove a collaborator**

Remove a user from a repository's collaborators, revoking the access granted to them directly. They keep any access they have through organization teams (or as anyone can, for public repositories). Use forgejo_list_collaborators to see who has access.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `username` | string | Yes | User name of the collaborator to remove |

### `forgejo_list_branch_protections`

**List branch protection rules**

List a repository's branch protection rules: who may push and merge (allowlists), required approvals, required status checks, review blockers, signed-commit requirement, protected file patterns and whether admins are bound too. Use forgejo_set_branch_protection to create or change a rule and forgejo_delete_branch_protection to remove one.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_set_branch_protection`

**Create or update a branch protection rule**

Create a branch protection rule, or update the existing rule with the same `rule_name` (only the settings you pass change). rule_name is a branch name or a glob pattern such as "main" or "release/*". A new rule with no other settings blocks direct pushes and force-pushes to matching branches. Configure push/merge/approval allowlists, required approvals, required status checks, review blockers, signed commits and protected files. Use forgejo_list_branch_protections to see current rules.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (idempotent update)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `rule_name` | string | Yes | Branch name or glob pattern the rule applies to, e.g. "main" or "release/*" |
| `enable_push` | boolean | No | Allow direct pushes to matching branches. New rules default to false: nobody can push directly, so changes go through pull requests |
| `enable_push_whitelist` | boolean | No | With pushing enabled, only the users/teams in the push allowlist may push |
| `push_whitelist_usernames` | string[] | No | Users allowed to push (replaces the current list). Implies enable_push and enable_push_whitelist |
| `push_whitelist_teams` | string[] | No | Teams allowed to push, organization repositories only (replaces the current list) |
| `push_whitelist_deploy_keys` | boolean | No | Also let deploy keys with write access push (part of the push allowlist) |
| `enable_merge_whitelist` | boolean | No | Only the users/teams in the merge allowlist may merge pull requests into matching branches |
| `merge_whitelist_usernames` | string[] | No | Users allowed to merge (replaces the current list). Implies enable_merge_whitelist |
| `merge_whitelist_teams` | string[] | No | Teams allowed to merge, organization repositories only (replaces the current list) |
| `required_approvals` | integer | No | Approving reviews needed before a pull request can be merged (0 = none) |
| `enable_approvals_whitelist` | boolean | No | Only count approvals from the users/teams in the approvals allowlist |
| `approvals_whitelist_username` | string[] | No | Users whose approvals count (replaces the current list). Implies enable_approvals_whitelist |
| `approvals_whitelist_teams` | string[] | No | Teams whose approvals count, organization repositories only (replaces the current list) |
| `enable_status_check` | boolean | No | Require commit status checks (CI) to pass before merging |
| `status_check_contexts` | string[] | No | Status check contexts that must pass; glob patterns allowed, e.g. "ci/build" or "ci/*". Implies enable_status_check |
| `block_on_rejected_reviews` | boolean | No | Block merging while the pull request has a "request changes" review |
| `block_on_official_review_requests` | boolean | No | Block merging while official review requests are still pending |
| `block_on_outdated_branch` | boolean | No | Block merging while the pull request branch is behind the base branch |
| `dismiss_stale_approvals` | boolean | No | Dismiss existing approvals when new commits are pushed |
| `ignore_stale_approvals` | boolean | No | Do not count approvals made on older commits (without dismissing them) |
| `require_signed_commits` | boolean | No | Reject pushes containing unsigned or unverifiable commits |
| `protected_file_patterns` | string | No | Files nobody may change by push, as semicolon-separated globs (e.g. ".forgejo/workflows/**;LICENSE"); "" clears it |
| `unprotected_file_patterns` | string | No | Files users with write access may push directly even when pushing is restricted, semicolon-separated globs; "" clears it |
| `apply_to_admins` | boolean | No | Apply the rule to repository administrators too |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_delete_branch_protection`

**Delete a branch protection rule**

Delete a branch protection rule by its rule name (e.g. "main" or "release/*"). Matching branches lose all of the rule's restrictions (anyone with write access can push and force-push). Use forgejo_list_branch_protections to find rule names.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `rule_name` | string | Yes | Exact rule name to delete, as shown by forgejo_list_branch_protections |

### `forgejo_list_webhooks`

**List repository webhooks**

List a repository's webhooks: ID, type, target URL, events, active state, branch filter and last update. Secrets and authorization headers are never shown, and tokens embedded in target URLs are masked. Use forgejo_create_webhook to add one and forgejo_delete_webhook to remove one.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_create_webhook`

**Create a repository webhook**

Add a webhook that makes Forgejo POST to a URL when events happen in the repository (push by default). `type` picks the payload format: "forgejo" (generic JSON or form) or a service integration (Slack needs extra_config.channel). Only pass `secret` or `authorization_header` if the user explicitly provided them; never invent one. They are stored by Forgejo and never shown again. Set `test` to send a test push event right away. Use forgejo_list_webhooks to review webhooks and forgejo_delete_webhook to remove one.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (creates something)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `url` | string | Yes | Target URL Forgejo sends the events to |
| `type` | `forgejo` \| `gitea` \| `gogs` \| `slack` \| `discord` \| `dingtalk` \| `telegram` \| `msteams` \| `feishu` \| `wechatwork` \| `packagist` | No | Payload format: "forgejo" (default), "gitea", "gogs", or a service: slack, discord, dingtalk, telegram, msteams, feishu, wechatwork, packagist. Default: `"forgejo"`. |
| `content_type` | `json` \| `form` | No | Body encoding for forgejo/gitea/gogs payloads: "json" (default) or "form". Default: `"json"`. |
| `events` | string[] | No | Events that trigger it (default ["push"]). Common: push, create, delete, fork, issues, issue_comment, pull_request, pull_request_review, pull_request_sync, release, wiki, repository, package. "issues" and "pull_request" include their sub-events (assign, label, milestone, comment) Default: `["push"]`. |
| `branch_filter` | string | No | Only fire push/create/delete events for matching branches, glob syntax (e.g. "main" or "{main,release/*}"). Default: all branches |
| `active` | boolean | No | Activate the webhook immediately (default true) Default: `true`. |
| `secret` | string | No | Secret for signing payloads (signature headers). ONLY pass a secret the user explicitly gave you |
| `authorization_header` | string | No | Authorization header value sent with every delivery, e.g. "Bearer <token>". ONLY pass one the user explicitly gave you |
| `extra_config` | object (map) | No | Type-specific settings, e.g. Slack {"channel": "#dev", "username": "forgejo"}; Packagist {"username", "api_token", "package_url"} |
| `test` | boolean | No | Send a test push event right after creating the webhook. Default: `false`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_delete_webhook`

**Delete a repository webhook**

Delete a repository webhook by its numeric ID; the target stops receiving events and the delivery history is lost. Use forgejo_list_webhooks to find the ID.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `id` | integer | Yes | Webhook ID, as shown by forgejo_list_webhooks |

### `forgejo_list_push_mirrors`

**List push mirrors**

List a repository's push mirrors (remotes Forgejo pushes to, e.g. a GitHub copy): remote name, remote address, sync interval, sync-on-commit, branch filter, last sync time and last error. Use forgejo_sync_mirror to push now, forgejo_create_push_mirror to add one and forgejo_delete_push_mirror to remove one.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_create_push_mirror`

**Create a push mirror**

Make Forgejo push this repository to another Git remote on a schedule and/or after every commit, e.g. to keep a GitHub copy in sync. Authenticate with `remote_username` + `remote_password` (for GitHub: your user name and a personal access token with write access), or with `use_ssh` (Forgejo generates a key pair; add the returned public key on the remote as a deploy key with write access). Only pass credentials the user explicitly provided; never invent them. They are stored by Forgejo and never shown again. Use forgejo_sync_mirror to push immediately and forgejo_list_push_mirrors to check the result.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (creates something)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `remote_address` | string | Yes | Target repository URL, e.g. https://github.com/owner/repo.git (or an SSH address like git@github.com:owner/repo.git with use_ssh) |
| `remote_username` | string | No | User name on the remote. ONLY pass credentials the user explicitly gave you |
| `remote_password` | string | No | Password or access token for the remote (needs remote_username). ONLY pass a token the user explicitly gave you |
| `use_ssh` | boolean | No | Authenticate with an SSH key pair generated by Forgejo instead of a password (the public key is returned) Default: `false`. |
| `interval` | string | No | Scheduled push interval as a duration like "8h0m0s" (default) or "1h30m" (instance minimum is usually 10m); "0" disables scheduled pushes. Default: `"8h0m0s"`. |
| `sync_on_commit` | boolean | No | Also push whenever new commits arrive (default true) Default: `true`. |
| `branch_filter` | string | No | Only mirror matching branches, glob syntax (e.g. "main" or "{main,release/*}"). Default: all branches |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_delete_push_mirror`

**Delete a push mirror**

Remove a push mirror by its remote name, so Forgejo stops pushing to that remote (the remote repository itself is not touched). Use forgejo_list_push_mirrors to find the remote name.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `remote_name` | string | Yes | Remote name of the push mirror, as shown by forgejo_list_push_mirrors (e.g. "remote_mirror_abc123") |

### `forgejo_sync_mirror`

**Sync mirrors now**

Trigger mirror synchronisation now instead of waiting for the schedule. which: "pull" fetches from the source of a pull-mirror repository (one created with forgejo_migrate_repo mirror: true), "push" pushes to all push mirrors, "both" (default) does both and reports which parts applied. Syncs run in the background: check forgejo_list_push_mirrors (last sync / last error) or forgejo_get_repo afterwards.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (creates something)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | Repository owner: a user or organization name (e.g. "aliff") |
| `repo` | string | Yes | Repository name (e.g. "my-project") |
| `which` | `pull` \| `push` \| `both` | No | "pull" (fetch from the source), "push" (push to all push mirrors) or "both" (default) Default: `"both"`. |

## packages

Package registry.

### `forgejo_list_packages`

**List packages**

List the packages of a user or organization in the Forgejo package registry: one row per package version, with type, name, version, creation date and linked repository. Filter by `type` (e.g. "npm", "container") and search by name with `query`. Use forgejo_get_package for a version's files and checksums.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | User or organization that owns the packages (e.g. "aliff") |
| `type` | string | No | Only this package type: one of alpine, cargo, chef, composer, conan, conda, container, cran, debian, generic, go, helm, maven, npm, nuget, pub, pypi, rpm, rubygems, swift, vagrant (or another type the instance supports) |
| `query` | string | No | Search text matched against package names |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_get_package`

**Get a package version**

Get one version of a package: who published it and when, its linked repository and web page, and its files with sizes and SHA-256 checksums. Use forgejo_list_packages to find the owner, type, name and version.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | User or organization that owns the packages (e.g. "aliff") |
| `type` | string | Yes | Package type: one of alpine, cargo, chef, composer, conan, conda, container, cran, debian, generic, go, helm, maven, npm, nuget, pub, pypi, rpm, rubygems, swift, vagrant (or another type the instance supports) |
| `name` | string | Yes | Package name as shown by forgejo_list_packages (e.g. "my-lib", "@scope/pkg" or "org/image") |
| `version` | string | Yes | Package version, e.g. "1.2.0" (for container images: the tag, e.g. "latest") |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_delete_package_version`

**Delete a package version**

Permanently delete one version of a package (and its files) from the package registry. Other versions are kept; anything that depends on this version will no longer be able to download it. Find versions with forgejo_list_packages.

- **Behaviour:** Destructive (deletes or irreversibly changes data; clients should ask first)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | Yes | User or organization that owns the packages (e.g. "aliff") |
| `type` | string | Yes | Package type: one of alpine, cargo, chef, composer, conan, conda, container, cran, debian, generic, go, helm, maven, npm, nuget, pub, pypi, rpm, rubygems, swift, vagrant (or another type the instance supports) |
| `name` | string | Yes | Package name as shown by forgejo_list_packages (e.g. "my-lib", "@scope/pkg" or "org/image") |
| `version` | string | Yes | Package version, e.g. "1.2.0" (for container images: the tag, e.g. "latest") |

## admin

Site administration (instance admins only).

### `forgejo_admin_list_users`

**List all users (admin)**

Site admins only: list every user account on the instance with email, admin flag, active/restricted state, last login and creation date. Filter by authentication source (source_id, login_name) and sort. Non-admins get HTTP 403; to find users by name use forgejo_search_users (users toolset) instead.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source_id` | integer | No | Only users of this authentication source ID (LDAP, OAuth2, ...) |
| `login_name` | string | No | Only the user with this exact login name at their authentication source (e.g. an LDAP uid) |
| `sort` | `oldest` \| `newest` \| `alphabetically` \| `reversealphabetically` \| `recentupdate` \| `leastupdate` | No | Sort order (default: the instance default, alphabetical) |
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 20; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `20`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_admin_list_cron_tasks`

**List cron tasks (admin)**

Site admins only: list the instance's scheduled maintenance tasks (mirror updates, repository health checks, cleanups, ...) with their schedule, next and previous run and how often they have run. Use the task name with forgejo_admin_run_cron_task to run one now. Non-admins get HTTP 403.

- **Behaviour:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | integer | No | Page number, starting at 1. Default: `1`. |
| `limit` | integer | No | Items per page (default 50; the instance caps this, usually at 50) Default: `50`. |
| `response_format` | `markdown` \| `json` | No | "markdown" (default) for a readable summary, or "json" for compact structured data. Default: `"markdown"`. |

### `forgejo_admin_run_cron_task`

**Run a cron task now (admin)**

Site admins only: start one of the instance's scheduled maintenance tasks immediately (e.g. "update_mirrors", "repo_health_check", "delete_old_actions"). It runs in the background; check forgejo_admin_list_cron_tasks afterwards for the updated previous-run time. Get valid task names from forgejo_admin_list_cron_tasks. Non-admins get HTTP 403.

- **Behaviour:** Writes (creates something)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string | Yes | Task name as listed by forgejo_admin_list_cron_tasks, e.g. "update_mirrors" |
